privacy: Allowlisted metrics, public metadata, and command templates only. No personal absolute paths, raw output, media, transcript text or fingerprints, speaker IDs, or raw provider responses.

release_packaging.scope: The final performance matrix measured this exact packaged executable. Debug symbols were stripped and the executable was signed again; every file-backed program section is byte-identical across this packaging step. Whole-file SHA changed because packaging changed. Workflow acceptance is recorded separately.

limitations: Results apply to these synthetic fixtures and this Apple Silicon execution environment, not every video or computer.
Cold means a fresh analysis directory, not a flushed OS disk cache. Runs are serial; no direct energy, temperature, or responsiveness telemetry was collected.
wait4 CPU includes waited-for descendants; max RSS is the kernel high-water measure, not summed simultaneous process-tree memory.
Same requested task sequence does not imply identical total internal work, global-index coverage, overview target timestamps, or semantic visual coverage.

The synthetic matrix's slides fixture has authored sidecar text but no voice samples because sandboxed say emitted empty audio. That matrix does not evaluate ASR accuracy or inference speed; separately allowlisted real local transcription workflows retain their own limitations.
Current harness hashes identify reproduction code at export time, not necessarily the script revision used for earlier preserved runs.
VideoToolbox failed inside sandbox but succeeded outside it. The initial invalid pixel-format experiment is retained only as iteration history, not as hardware evidence.

fixtures.name: slides
fixtures.purpose: Readable slides, progressive reveals, chart change, and local synthesized speech with exact cue boundaries; not an ASR accuracy benchmark.

fixtures.name: motion
fixtures.purpose: Sixty decoded frames per second with continuously moving shapes and a long GOP; tests dense frame adjacency and late seeking.

fixtures.name: scale
fixtures.purpose: Two-minute continuous visual motion to expose duration-dependent full-decode preparation cost.

fixtures.name: vfr
fixtures.purpose: Two frame rates in one timeline; average-FPS arithmetic must not replace decoded timestamps.

fixtures.name: offset
fixtures.purpose: Decoded timestamps begin at five seconds, testing input seeking and absolute timeline labels.

fixtures.name: rotation
fixtures.purpose: Ninety-degree display matrix on the same high-rate footage; display geometry must respect rotation.
fixtures.correction: Unrotated duplicate generated by ignored legacy rotation metadata; excluded from actual rotation claims and corrected comparisons.

fixtures.name: rotation_verified
fixtures.purpose: Verified 90-degree display matrix; corrects the legacy metadata command that silently produced an unrotated duplicate.

decisions.theory: Bound decoder, filter and encoder worker counts to two
decisions.reason: Balances response latency and memory pressure. On 1080p60, one/two/four threads measured 1.130/0.622/0.343 seconds and 42.6/58.4/90.3 MiB. Two threads is not minimum elapsed time.
Approximately doubles sparse decode latency versus two threads on both fixtures; lower memory remains a possible explicit low-resource mode.
Cuts latency, but raises simultaneous compute and peak RSS; conflicts with quiet default. An explicit throughput setting remains possible.

decisions.theory: Use one bounded seek/decode for dense ranges
decisions.reason: 13-frame output: 0.162 seconds and 0.319 CPU seconds versus 1.987 seconds and 3.416 CPU seconds for separate seeks; all JPEGs and PTS identical.

decisions.theory: Use separate seek per sparse target for every clip
decisions.reason: 18-second source whole-span extraction was 2.4x faster and used half the CPU. On a two-minute source separate seeks instead reduced CPU from 2.122 to 1.327 seconds. Select strategy from span density.

decisions.theory: Use fixed groups of three for all sparse clips
decisions.reason: On two-minute fixture, groups were slower and used more CPU than individual seeks. Grouping should follow temporal spacing, not fixed count alone.

Hardware succeeded outside sandbox with matching output, but was about 4.1x slower for this sparse task despite lower host CPU. Hardware initialization failure inside sandbox does not establish a Mac capability limit.

720px reduced 12-frame artifacts from 1,006,781 to 337,159 bytes and RSS from 58.4 to 45.2 MiB; no clear decode-latency gain. Choose final width after readability review; keep full-resolution inspection available.

decisions.theory: Replace Lanczos with area or bilinear globally
decisions.reason: Observed wall differences overlap repeat jitter. No substantial latency benefit established; visual/readability quality must govern any scaler change.

corrections: Initial fixture named rotation was an unrotated duplicate because FFmpeg ignored legacy rotate metadata; original files and results frozen, verified 90-degree fixture added separately.

Initial hardware experiment used an invalid output pixel-format name; corrected videotoolbox_vld run still failed inside sandbox. Unsandboxed corrected run succeeded, and all 36 hardware/software JPEG pairs were SHA256 identical.
Local say under sandbox emitted no speech samples. Slides fixture has authored sidecar but no voice audio, and cannot substantiate ASR accuracy or inference-speed claims.
